topic: What people built with Grok 4.6 in 48 hours
angle: The gap between a model launching and people shipping with it is now two days
hook: People built this with Grok 4.6 in 48 hours
caption:
Grok 4.6 landed less than two days ago and the demos are already past the toy stage. Playable games, navigable 3D worlds, and files that came out of an actual 3D printer. The interesting part is not the model — it is that the gap between a release and people shipping real things with it has collapsed to about a weekend.

💬 Comment "GROK" and I'll send you the full list.
🔖 Save this for the next time you need it.

slides.text: People built this with Grok 4.6 in *48 hours*
slides.subline: Games, 3D worlds, and real printed objects

slides.text: A model launches. Two days later people have shipped things with it. That loop used to take a year.

slides.title: Playable games
slides.body: Not screenshots of games. Working ones, generated and running in a browser, built by people who describe what they want rather than writing the engine themselves.

slides.title: Objects you can hold
slides.body: Some of the output went to a 3D printer and came back as a physical thing. The model produced the file. That is the part worth paying attention to.

slides.left_text: A model drops. You read the benchmark thread and move on.
slides.right_text: A model drops. By Monday someone shipped a product on it.

slides.title: What to actually do
slides.body: Do not read another benchmark table. Pick one thing you have wanted to build for a year and spend an evening describing it to the model. The bar for a first version has never been lower.
